checks: No eclipse at 6 of 25 covered epochs where the 1.04115 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 272885856 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.0411 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing a 0.03% dimming of the star's light, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 19.9 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms the signal originates near the target location, though with a centroid offset of 7.7 arcseconds and a peak signal-to-noise of 5.1. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel target. The automated pipeline's machine learning classifier assigned it a score of 0.61, indicating moderate confidence in its authenticity. This candidate passed all data quality checks without flagging any concerns.
